value_types.langstring: A string that may carry a language tag.
value_types.uri: An absolute URI, serialised as a node reference not a string.
value_types.bytes: A non-negative integer count of bytes.
value_types.media_type: An IANA media type, or a format token where none exists.
value_types.agent: A person or organisation; a node with at least a name.
value_types.concept: A term from a controlled scheme; prefer its URI.
value_types.location: A place; prefer a resolvable URI over a name string.
value_types.period: A time interval, expressed as start and end.
value_types.frequency: A term from the Dublin Core Frequency vocabulary.
value_types.checksum: A hash digest, with its algorithm.
value_types.vcard: A contact, serialised as a vCard node.
value_types.structured: A nested object whose shape the standard defines.

directions.both: Read on import, write on export.
directions.export_only: Platform-derived. Emit it; never let an import overwrite it.
directions.import_only: Accept from a source; the platform does not re-emit it.
directions.none: Platform-internal. Not metadata; ignore in both directions.

language.notes: ISO 639-1 code appended to the scheme

identifier.label: Identifier
identifier.definition: A unique identifier for the dataset (platform ID, DOI, catalog UUID).
identifier.notes: Croissant uses @id for this. On import the incoming identifier is kept in source_identifier, never written over the platform's own ID.

source_identifier.label: Source identifier
source_identifier.definition: The identifier this dataset carried on the platform it was imported from.
source_identifier.notes: Not in the source workbook. Added because round-tripping a federated record is impossible without somewhere to keep its origin ID.

slug.label: Slug
slug.definition: URL-safe short name for the dataset on the platform.
slug.notes: No standard equivalent; it is the path component of landing_page.

title.label: Title
title.definition: A name given to the dataset.

alternative_title.label: Alternative title
alternative_title.definition: An alternative name for the dataset.

description.label: Description
description.definition: A free-text account of the dataset.

abstract.label: Abstract
abstract.definition: A summary of the dataset, shorter than the description.

keyword.label: Keywords
keyword.definition: Free-text tags describing the dataset, used for search.

theme.label: Theme / Sector
theme.definition: The category the dataset belongs to, from a controlled scheme.
theme.notes: Partial match. CDL sectors are the platform's own scheme; export maps them onto EU data themes, which collapses several sectors onto one theme.

dataset_type.label: Dataset type
dataset_type.definition: The nature or genre of the dataset.
dataset_type.notes: The platform's set of types is undefined in the source workbook.

language.label: Language
language.definition: Language of the dataset, as an ISO 639 code or URI.
language.notes: Requires normalisation to ISO codes/URIs on import.

publisher.label: Publisher
publisher.definition: The entity responsible for making the dataset available.
publisher.notes: The workbook maps organization to dct:publisher but Croissant creator, and user to dct:creator but Croissant publisher. That inversion is preserved here as recorded; see the open question in the README.

creator.label: Creator
creator.definition: The entity responsible for producing the dataset.

qualified_attribution.label: Qualified attribution
qualified_attribution.definition: A role-qualified link to an agent, for multiple contributors.
qualified_attribution.notes: Needed when a dataset has several publishers with distinct roles.

contact_point.label: Contact point
contact_point.definition: Contact information for the dataset, as a vCard.
contact_point.notes: Sub-fields are the contact_* concepts on the contact_point node.

license.label: License
license.definition: The legal document under which the dataset is made available.
license.notes: Must serialise as a resolvable LicenseDocument URI, not the enum label. Resolve through the license vocabulary before emitting.

rights.label: Rights statement
rights.definition: A statement about rights held in and over the dataset.

access_rights.label: Access rights
access_rights.definition: Whether the dataset is public, restricted, or non-public.
access_rights.notes: The workbook calls accessType unclear and marks it unmappable. It lines up with dcterms:accessRights if it means public/restricted; confirm against the platform before relying on this binding.

issued.label: Date issued
issued.definition: The date the dataset was first published.
issued.notes: The platform's "created" is mapped to issued, not dcterms:created. The workbook flags that it is unclear whether this is the original creation date or the upload date.

created.label: Date created
created.definition: The date the dataset itself was created, before publication.

modified.label: Date modified
modified.definition: The most recent date the dataset was changed.
modified.notes: Should be driven by the platform's versioning, per the workbook.

accrual_periodicity.label: Update frequency
accrual_periodicity.definition: How often the dataset is updated.
accrual_periodicity.notes: Use the Dublin Core Frequency vocabulary.

accrual_method.label: Accrual method
accrual_method.definition: How the dataset is added to.

version.label: Version
version.definition: The version designator of the dataset.
version.notes: DCAT has no single version field; the workbook records the combination of issued + modified + dcterms:hasVersion as the partial match.

spatial_coverage.label: Spatial coverage
spatial_coverage.definition: The geographic region the dataset covers.
spatial_coverage.notes: Must serialise as a resolvable place URI. The platform stores name strings today; resolve through the geography vocabulary first.

spatial_resolution.label: Spatial resolution
spatial_resolution.definition: Minimum spatial separation resolvable in the dataset.
spatial_resolution.notes: DCAT expects metres. The registry sheet uses admin level (district, village), which needs a conversion or a separate literal field.

temporal_coverage_start.label: Temporal coverage (start)
temporal_coverage_start.definition: Start of the period the dataset covers.
temporal_coverage_start.notes: Serialises inside a dcterms:temporal PeriodOfTime node.

temporal_coverage_end.label: Temporal coverage (end)
temporal_coverage_end.definition: End of the period the dataset covers.

temporal_resolution.label: Temporal resolution
temporal_resolution.definition: Minimum time period resolvable in the dataset.

landing_page.label: Landing page
landing_page.definition: A web page giving access to the dataset and its publisher.
landing_page.notes: Constructed from slug at export time.

homepage.label: Homepage
homepage.definition: The publisher's home page for the dataset.

source.label: Source
source.definition: A related resource the dataset is derived from.

in_catalog.label: In catalog
in_catalog.definition: The catalog the dataset is listed in.

in_series.label: In series
in_series.definition: The dataset series this dataset belongs to.

conforms_to.label: Conforms to
conforms_to.definition: An established standard or schema the dataset conforms to.
conforms_to.notes: Unbound. Definition values export by concept through metadata_mapping.py.

relation.label: Related resource
relation.definition: A resource with an unspecified relationship to the dataset.

has_part.label: Has part
has_part.definition: A resource included either physically or logically in the dataset.

is_part_of.label: Is part of
is_part_of.definition: A resource the dataset is included in.

is_referenced_by.label: Is referenced by
is_referenced_by.definition: A resource that references the dataset.

is_replaced_by.label: Is replaced by
is_replaced_by.definition: A resource that supplants the dataset.

is_version_of.label: Is version of
is_version_of.definition: A resource the dataset is a version of.

provenance.label: Provenance
provenance.definition: A statement of changes in ownership and custody of the dataset.
provenance.notes: DCAT needs the external PROV-O ontology for this.

jurisdiction_level.label: Jurisdiction level
jurisdiction_level.definition: The administrative level the dataset's authority operates at.
jurisdiction_level.notes: DCAT-IN, not yet a stable published spec.

applicable_legislation.label: Applicable legislation
applicable_legislation.definition: The legislation mandating the dataset's creation or publication.

hvd_category.label: High-value dataset category
hvd_category.definition: The high-value dataset category the dataset falls in.

note.label: Note
note.definition: A free-text note about the dataset.

distribution.label: Distribution
distribution.definition: An accessible form of the dataset — a downloadable file or an API.
distribution.notes: The link from dataset to its distribution nodes.

access_url.label: Access URL
access_url.definition: A URL giving access to the distribution.
access_url.notes: DCAT requires this on every Distribution. Where the platform has only a download URL, use it for both.

download_url.label: Download URL
download_url.definition: A direct link to the downloadable file.

media_type.label: Format / media type
media_type.definition: The file format of the distribution.
media_type.notes: The platform's dataset-level "formats" is the set of its resources' formats, derived rather than entered.

byte_size.label: Byte size
byte_size.definition: The size of the distribution in bytes.

checksum.label: Checksum
checksum.definition: A hash of the distribution's contents, for integrity checking.
checksum.notes: Croissant requires sha256 on a FileObject; DCAT has no such property.

distribution_title.label: Distribution title
distribution_title.definition: A name given to the distribution.

endpoint_url.label: Endpoint URL
endpoint_url.definition: The root location of an API-based distribution.

endpoint_description.label: Endpoint description
endpoint_description.definition: A description of the services available at the endpoint.

file_set.label: File set
file_set.definition: A group of files described by a pattern rather than individually.
file_set.notes: DCAT has no grouping semantics; the nearest is many Distributions.

containment.label: Containment
containment.definition: Which file or archive a file is contained in.

record_set.label: Record set
record_set.definition: A table within the dataset — its columns and their semantics.
record_set.notes: The main DCAT gap. This is the concept that makes a dataset ML-readable, and it is also what schemas/data_dictionary_template.csv captures.

field.label: Field
field.definition: One column of a record set, with a name, description and type.
field.notes: No column-level metadata exists in DCAT.

data_type.label: Data type
data_type.definition: The semantic type of a field (including ML types like BoundingBox).

transform.label: Transform
transform.definition: A transformation applied to source data to produce a field.
transform.notes: Expressible in DCAT only through external PROV-O.

annotation.label: Annotation
annotation.definition: A structured ML annotation over the data.

contact_role.label: Contact role
contact_role.definition: Role the contact plays for this dataset.

contact_address.label: Contact address
contact_address.notes: Nests the contact_street_address / locality / postal_code concepts.

contact_locality.label: Contact locality
contact_locality.definition: Town or city of the contact's address.

contact_postal_code.label: Contact postal code
contact_postal_code.definition: Postal code of the contact's address.

status.label: Status
status.definition: Publication workflow state of the dataset on the platform.
status.notes: Croissant has a status concept; the workbook records no DCAT equivalent and marks it not user-facing.

download_count.label: Download count
download_count.definition: Number of times the dataset has been downloaded.
download_count.notes: Usage statistic, not metadata. No DCAT equivalent.

similar_datasets.label: Similar datasets
similar_datasets.definition: Datasets the platform computes as related.
similar_datasets.notes: Platform-level and dynamic; the workbook says it need not be metadata.

is_individual_dataset.label: Is individual dataset
is_individual_dataset.definition: Whether the record is a standalone dataset or part of a collection.
is_individual_dataset.notes: The workbook suspects this links to catalogs. If confirmed, it belongs with in_catalog / in_series rather than here.

dataspace.label: Dataspace
dataspace.notes: Marked unclear and unmappable in the source workbook.

citation.label: Citation
citation.definition: How to cite the dataset, as free text (BibTeX or a sentence).
citation.notes: Croissant citeAs; Dublin Core / DCAT dcterms:bibliographicCitation.

dcat:keyword.notes: dcat:keyword or dcterms:subject, depending on whether the values are free text or come from a controlled scheme. The platform's tags are semi-controlled, so keyword is the safer target.

dcat:theme.notes: Expects a skos:Concept from a published scheme. CDL sectors collapse onto EU data themes many-to-one; the mapping is lossy in that direction and not reversible.

dcterms:type.notes: Dataset-level only. DCAT has no field-level typing.

prov:qualifiedAttribution.notes: Requires PROV-O, which is outside DCAT proper.

dcat:contactPoint.notes: Nests a vcard:Kind node built from the contact_* concepts.

dcterms:license.notes: Mandatory at Distribution in the registry profile. Emit the steward URI from the license vocabulary, never the platform's enum label.

dcterms:accessRights.notes: Croissant has no equivalent; this is DCAT-only.

owl:versionInfo.notes: DCAT has no dedicated version field. The workbook records the combination issued + modified + dcterms:hasVersion / owl:versionInfo. owl:versionInfo is used here because dcterms:hasVersion means "a version of this exists over there" - binding both concepts to it would make an incoming hasVersion impossible to route.

dcat:spatialResolutionInMeters.notes: DCAT wants metres. The registry records admin level instead, which does not convert cleanly — carry it as a literal or drop it.

dcterms:conformsTo.notes: DCAT's only way to point at an external schema such as CSVW.

dcatin:jurisdictionLevel.notes: DCAT-IN, proposed. Namespace is a placeholder until it publishes.

dcat:mediaType.notes: dcterms:format is the looser alternative the workbook also records. Use mediaType when the value is a real MIME type, format otherwise.

gaps.notes: No integrity-verification property in DCAT. Croissant requires sha256.
No file grouping or pattern support; nearest is many Distributions.
Cannot represent tables or rows. Use conforms_to to point outward.
Publication workflow state is not a DCAT concept.

export.notes: Dublin Core has no free-text keyword element. subject is the nearest and is meant to carry controlled terms, so round-tripping tags through it loses the distinction between a tag and a theme.

Shares dcterms:subject with keyword. On import from Dublin Core there is no way to tell which concept a subject value belongs to; the workbook's DCAT sheet maps Subject to both dcat:theme and dcat:keyword for the same reason. Prefer DCAT when the distinction matters.
Dublin Core has no start/end structure - temporal takes a single literal period. Serialise start and end as one DCMI Period string; parsing it back into two dates is best-effort.
See temporal_coverage_start; both concepts share one property.
Dublin Core has no download link. The workbook's Identifier row maps to dcat:landingPage and foaf:homePage for this reason. Lossy either way.
Flattened onto the dataset, because Dublin Core has no Distribution. For a multi-file dataset this collapses to the set of its formats.
Flattened onto the dataset; a literal, not a byte count.

dcterms:identifier.notes: Dublin Core has no download link. The workbook's Identifier row maps to dcat:landingPage and foaf:homePage for this reason. Lossy either way.

dcterms:subject.notes: Dublin Core has no free-text keyword element. subject is the nearest and is meant to carry controlled terms, so round-tripping tags through it loses the distinction between a tag and a theme.

Shares dcterms:subject with keyword. On import from Dublin Core there is no way to tell which concept a subject value belongs to; the workbook's DCAT sheet maps Subject to both dcat:theme and dcat:keyword for the same reason. Prefer DCAT when the distinction matters.

dcterms:temporal.notes: Dublin Core has no start/end structure - temporal takes a single literal period. Serialise start and end as one DCMI Period string; parsing it back into two dates is best-effort.
See temporal_coverage_start; both concepts share one property.

dcterms:provenance.notes: A free-text statement, not the structured PROV-O graph.

dcterms:format.notes: Flattened onto the dataset, because Dublin Core has no Distribution. For a multi-file dataset this collapses to the set of its formats.

dcterms:extent.notes: Flattened onto the dataset; a literal, not a byte count.

gaps.notes: No contact structure; publisher is the only agent-ish element.
No version element. dcterms:hasVersion points at a different resource that is a version of this one, which is has_version, not this concept.
No Distribution resource. Every file-level fact flattens or is lost.
No homepage term in DCMI Metadata Terms.
